examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
examples.problem: Express $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u+v) = \sin{u}\cos{v} + \cos{u}\sin{v}
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={330}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{330}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{330}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{330}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
